SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Schedule J, Part I, Line 7 Non-fixed payments
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The HOS compensation structure includes an annual discretionary bonus that can be awarded in an amount commensurate with predefined performance benchmarks up to a maximum limit of $100,000. Benchmarks vary from year to year, dependent upon the agenda for the HOS and are agreed upon between the HOS and Board, but may include leadership of administrative team, fundraising, facilities improvements, admissions/enrollment metrics, operational initiatives, and renewal/maintenance of accreditation. The HSEC reviews the performance of the HOS on an annual basis based upon these predetermined benchmarks and submits a recommendation regarding the amount of this discretionary bonus (if any) to the Board each year. Excepting members with a conflict of interest, the Board then votes on whether to approve the HSEC's recommended bonus.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 11b Review of form 990 by governing body
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: Form 990 is prepared by an independent CPA firm and reviewed in detail by the organization's top management. The reviewed Form 990 is then provided to the board of directors prior to filing with the IRS.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 12c Conflict of interest policy
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The organization requires all officers and board members to annually complete and sign a conflict of interest questionnaire. The Head of School/CEO, Board Chair, Vice Chair, and Secretary are responsible for reviewing the signed statements and ensuring that interested persons are in compliance with the conflict of interest policy. Should any potential conflicts of interest be disclosed, the board member or officer recuses himself or herself from participation in any deliberation or decision with regard to matters affected by the relationship.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 15a Process to establish compensation of top management official
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Board has an independent committee, the HSEC (Headmaster Support and Evaluation Committee), that is charged with evaluating and supporting the Head of School/CEO throughout the year and proposing compensation increases to the independent members of the Board for approval. During renewal of the employment contract, the HSEC determined that the existing HOS salary and overall compensation package was deficient when compared to other private secondary schools. Increases in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 were part of the school's long term succession planning, since integration of a market rate HOS salary into the budget is critical for recruitment and retention of a high caliber candidate. The HSEC hired an outside consultant to appropriately benchmark the HOS salary. The HOS's specific salary increases are in the middle range of those benchmark data.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 15b Process to establish compensation of other employees
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: The Head of School/CEO determines compensation for any other officers or key employees. Industry comparability data is used to determine compensation, and the process is documented as part of the annual review process and maintained in HR files.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: Form 990, Part VI, Line 19 Required documents available to the public
